I would like to receive any and all information that you have collected in collaboration on City of Wyoming on the listed public officials from January 1st, 2026 to present, September 20th, 2026. How many times their plates were captured, how many times they were searched, or any other information captured on these officials by the Flock citizen surveillance system. The public and the City Council are entitled to how they are being stalked, surveilled, and tracked by this system that is illegal under the 4th amendment, as well as the 6-3 Supreme Court decision of Chartrie vs US on July 26th, 2026.

Thank you for your time,
And I hope that you can complete my request as it was stated.

communications.subject: RE: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request #F26-825 MP
communications.communication:
Hello,

Your FOIA request was combined with a separate FOIA request received on the same day (September 4th, 2026). As a result, you may have received responsive records associated with the other FOIA request.

With respect to your request concerning City Council members, the information provided in response to your request is addressed on the second page of the FOIA response letter. The City of Wyoming does not maintain a record identifying the license plate numbers associated with City Council members.

As a result, the City is unable to identify or search for records based solely on the individual’s status as a City Council member. If you are seeking records associated with a specific vehicle, please provide the corresponding license plate number so that the City can conduct an appropriate record search.

If you have any questions, my contact information can be found below.

Thank you,

Monzerrat Perez
Office Specialist II, Records Unit｜Wyoming Police Department

communications.subject: RE: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request #F26-825 MP

I'm not a creep, I'm not going to stalk my fellow citizens to obtain their license plate numbers. I have a great deal of respect for our City Council and have had great pleasure in working with them. This request was to show the illegal power law enforcement has over us all. You guys have the power to creepily stalk all of us illegally under the 4th Amendment of the Constitution, as well as being illegal under the July 2026 Chatrie vs US Supreme Court decision 6-3. If you don't want to provide this information, I understand you have your orders. I will fix my second FOIA request you mentioned, and hope to get some real answers. 

Thank you for your time and detailed response,
Henry

title: ForwardEdge ASIC (City of Saint Paul, Minnesota - City Attorney)

communications.subject: Minnesota Government Data Practices Act Request: ForwardEdge ASIC (City of Saint Paul, Minnesota - City Attorney)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Minnesota Government Data Practices Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am requesting any records and documents and communications that pertain to or reference the company ForwardEdge ASIC located at 2340 Energy Park Drive, St Paul. This request also encompasses documents and records from any of ForwardEdge’s parent and subsidiary entities, to the extent they relate to any request below.
My request encompasses any documents and city communications which name ForwardEdge ASIC, including but not limited to:
(a) reports, slide decks, presentations, documents, or communications from ForwardEdge ASIC to the City of St. Paul (“the City”) regarding or referring to the Minnesota Investment Fund (“MIF”) loan
(b) any contracts signed between ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and the City
(c) any loan provided by the City to ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and any related reporting requirements the City imposed on the recipient
(d) any grant applications and grant application materials submitted to the City of St Paul by ForwardEdge ASIC, or any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, for the MIF loan
(e) any other applications that ForwardEdge ASIC has submitted to the City,
(f) records that show how much of the MIF loan funds have been dispersed as of the date of this request, and any expected distributions in the year 2026
(g) any other documents that refer to ForwardEdge ASIC.
(h) any communications between the city of Saint Paul and the Saint Paul Police Department regarding ForwardEdge ASIC.
(h) any email communications between ForwardEdge ASIC, on any entity on behalf of ForwardEdge ASIC, and the City between April 24, 2025 and Jul 13, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Arco Orca

communications.subject: Connecticut Freedom of Information Act Request: Citizen Services Bureau Requests
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Connecticut Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Record of all requests to the Citizen's Service Bureau from January 1 2023 to most recent in which the location of the requests  is in the Cove, East Side  or West Side in which the request has been open for 90 or more days or the request is closed and took 90 or more days to complete.

If these regions of the city are not available then include all requests in the 06902 area code. 

If the open or closed time information is not available then include all requests regardless of opening and closing date. 

Include the following fields or most similar field available : the data the request was submitted, the date the request was closed, the type of request, the mailing address of the request,  the current status of the request.

I also request that, if possible and pursuant to Conn. Gen. Stat. § 1-212(d), fees be waived as I believe this request is in the public interest and not made for commercial gain. The requested documents will be made available to the public at MuckRock.com.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 4 business days, as the statute requires.

communications.subject: RE: Michigan Freedom of Information Act Request: Nessel MFA emails
communications.communication:
Dear Ms. Estrada:
This letter is a written APPEAL of the fee assessed in the Department's August 18, 2026 notice regarding my FOIA request of August 11, 2026 number 217956 (Invoice #2026-046489-A / #2026-046489-B; Detailed Itemization form dated 8/19/26 lists these as #2026-0464890-A/B). I submit this appeal under MCL 15.240a(1)(a) and the Department's own FOIA Procedures and Guidelines. Because this appeal is being filed, MCL 15.234(14) does not require a deposit within 45 days of the notice; I ask that the Department instead issue the written determination required by MCL 15.240a(2) within 10 business days.
The Department's Detailed Itemization of Fees form assesses a total fee of $1,451.20 (deposit: $725.60), consisting entirely of Item 2, “Labor costs for review and examination of responsive records and the separation of exempt from non-exempt material” — 32 hours at $37.60/hour ($1,203.20) plus 32 hours of fringe benefits at $7.75/hour ($248.00). Every other fee component on the form — including Item 1, labor to search for and retrieve responsive records — is left blank, i.e., charged at $0. For the reasons below, this fee is not adequately substantiated and exceeds the amount permitted under MCL 15.234, and I ask that it be reduced.
1. The itemization does not “explain” the charge, as MCL 15.234(4) requires.
MCL 15.234(4) requires that a public body's detailed itemization “clearly list and explain the allowable charges” for each fee component. The form lists a bare figure — 32 hours — with no description of what that time represents: how many custodians' accounts were searched, how many messages or threads matched the *.gov.il criteria, what volume of records the Department expects to review, or what methodology (e.g., sampling of a test search) produced the 32-hour estimate. A number without an explanation of how it was derived does not satisfy the statute. I ask that the Department provide the underlying basis for the 32-hour figure — including the estimated number of responsive records or hits — so the estimate can be evaluated.
2. The fee is internally inconsistent: $0 in search/retrieval labor alongside a finding that the request is “voluminous.”
The Department's notice states that “a voluminous number of records falls within the scope of the FOIA request,” yet the itemization charges nothing for Item 1, the labor “to search for and retrieve responsive records” under MCL 15.234(1)(a). It is not apparent how the Department could determine that a request is voluminous without expending any search time, or how 32 hours of review time was calculated for a record set whose size was never estimated through a charged search. Under MCL 15.240a(4), the burden is on the public body to establish that a fee complies with MCL 15.234; this inconsistency indicates that burden has not been met for the fee as a whole, and I ask the Department to reconcile it.
3. The justification for charging review and examination costs is generic, not particular to this request, as MCL 15.234(3) requires.
A public body may charge for review, examination, and redaction only if “failure to charge a fee would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request in the particular instance, and the public body specifically identifies the nature of these unreasonably high costs.” MCL 15.234(3) (emphasis added). The notice's explanation — that “employees must be taken away from pending work to process the request and expend additional time to complete regularly assigned Departmental work” — is boilerplate that could be recited for any FOIA request the Department receives. It does not identify anything particular to this request (e.g., the specific number of custodians, mailboxes, or years of correspondence at issue) that makes its cost unreasonably high. I ask the Department to identify the request-specific facts supporting this charge.
4. The itemization does not identify the employee classification behind the $37.60 hourly rate.
MCL 15.234(1)(b) limits the review/redaction charge to “the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of separating and deleting exempt information from nonexempt information in the particular instance.” The form lists only a dollar figure, with no job title or classification, so I have no way to confirm that $37.60 reflects the Department's lowest-paid capable employee rather than a more convenient or higher rate. I ask that the Department identify the job classification associated with this rate.
Requested relief
I ask that the Department, within 10 business days as provided by MCL 15.240a(2):
•  Reduce the fee to an amount supported by a documented, request-specific basis for the estimated hours, or waive the deposit requirement pending that documentation;
•  Provide the estimated volume of responsive records or search hits underlying the 32-hour review estimate, and the job classification for the $37.60 hourly rate; and
•  Advise whether the Department would consider a further reduction in the public interest, given that the request concerns communications between a state law enforcement official and officials of a foreign government — a matter of substantial public concern — or would be willing to discuss a narrowed scope (e.g., a shorter date range or a defined set of custodians) that might reduce the processing burden without abandoning the request.
I am glad to discuss narrowing the request's scope with your office if that would help produce a more accurate, lower estimate. Please direct any response to 217956-87735259@requests.muckrock.com cc’d to
 matthew.petti@reason.com.
Sincerely,
Matthew Petti

Dear Ms. Estrada and Mr. Jamison:

Thank you for the Department's September 14, 2026 determination of my fee appeal. I appreciate the Department's disclosure that its search of all Department staff email accounts for messages to or from any address ending in “*.gov.il” located at least 1,260 items requiring review, and its suggestion that a request with a shorter date range or a defined set of custodians could reduce the processing burden and cost.
I am submitting this letter as a modified FOIA request, superseding and replacing request #217956 in its entirety. I ask that the Department treat request #217956 as withdrawn upon receipt of this modified request, with no further fee or deposit obligation outstanding on it, and process the narrower request below in its place.

Modified request

Pursuant to the Michigan Freedom of Information Act, MCL 15.231 et seq., I request emails sent to or received from any address ending in “*.gov.il,” including any attachments, from October 7, 2023 to the date this request is received, involving:
(1)  Attorney General Dana Nessel; and
(2)  whoever served, at any time during that period, in the following roles within the Attorney General's immediate executive office: Chief of Staff, Chief Deputy Attorney General, and Director of Communications / Public Information and Education (or the closest equivalent title if these positions have been renamed).
I do not have the names of every person who held these roles throughout the period, and ask that the Department identify and search the accounts of whoever occupied them at the relevant times. If it would help the Department scope this efficiently, I am glad to receive a current list of the individuals in these roles and confirm the search accordingly.

This is a small fraction of the custodians covered by the Department's original search of “all Department staff,” and a shorter window than the roughly four years and three months covered by my original request. Before any deposit is required, I ask that the Department provide an updated Detailed Itemization of Fees for this narrowed scope, including the estimated number of responsive items for these custodians and the job classification underlying the hourly rate charged for review, consistent with the level of detail the Department was able to provide in its September 14 determination.

As with my original request, these records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes. I would prefer the records provided electronically.

Sincerely,
Matthew Petti

title: William J. Clinton Presidential Library: WHTV Tapes of December 8th, 1999 meeting between Clinton and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: William J. Clinton Presidential Library: WHTV Tapes of December 8th, 1999 meeting between Clinton and Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am seeking access to specific audiovisual records maintained by the Clinton Presidential Library created by the White House Communications Agency (WHCA) and White House Television (WHTV).

According to previously released copies of Clinton's schedule on Wednesday, December 8th, 1999, President Clinton held a meeting with Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma in the Oval Office from 10:15 am to 10:45 am. While the schedule for that day notes "STILLS ONLY," photographic evidence confirms the presence of a formal photo opportunity. Standard operating procedure for WHCA during this era typically included a "WHTV Master" recording of such high-level diplomatic head-of-state meetings for archival and internal purposes.

For reference, here's a photograph from that day: 
https://photo.unian.info/photo/1348-leonid-kuchma-and-william-jefferson-bill-clinton

Specifically, I request:

Any WHCA/WHTV video recordings (including raw footage, pool spray footage, b-roll, or “photo opportunity” coverage) of:

The Oval Office meeting between President Clinton and President Kuchma.

Any associated press “spray,” press availability, or staged photo opportunity in the Oval Office or other White House locations on that date.

Any associated shot logs, tape logs, daily production logs, rundowns, or indices created by WHCA/WHTV for December 8, 1999, that reference:

"President Leonid Kuchma"

"Ukraine"

"Oval Office Meeting"

"WHTV Master" or "WHCA Video" logs for the 10:00 am – 11:00 am timeframe.

Format and Delivery:
I request that these records be provided in a digital format. If the video is located and cleared for release, I respectfully request that the Library consider uploading the digitized footage to the "ClintonLibrary42 YouTube channel" to ensure broad public access to this historical record of U.S.-Ukraine relations.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

title: RG 330: Research and Development Board finding aids, 1946–1953

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: RG 330: Research and Development Board finding aids, 1946–1953
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Existing finding aids and archival control records describing
Research and Development Board records within Record Group 330,
Records of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, for any portion
of January 1, 1946, through December 31, 1953.

Please route this request to the reference/access staff responsible
for these RG 330 holdings and, as appropriate, the office responsible
for FOIA processing.

Please provide existing inventories, series descriptions, entry
lists, box and folder lists, file-classification guides, and subject
or project indexes for these holdings described in section 330.11.3
of NARA's Guide to Federal Records:

1. Records concerning fiscal and budgetary aspects of research and
development programs, described as covering 1946–1953.

2. Executive Council meeting minutes, described as covering
1946–1950.

3. Committee on Technical Information records, described as covering
1946–1953.

Please include existing indexes or registers identifying research
projects or studies represented in these specific holdings, together
with any accompanying keys or guides needed to interpret their
file codes.

The date range applies to the underlying historical records, not
to when the finding aids were prepared. Existing aids spanning
additional years may be supplied without creating a new version.

This request seeks existing descriptive and indexing records,
not copies of all underlying program files, minutes, or technical
reports and not the creation of a new research-project inventory.

Please include archival identifiers and access-restriction
information already contained in the requested aids.

If the materials are openly available, please provide them through
ordinary reference access or supply direct links to the specific
aids. Please process remaining restricted responsive records under
FOIA as applicable.

Please release reasonably segregable nonexempt portions and identify
any exemptions applied. Electronic delivery through MuckRock is
preferred. I authorize fees up to $25 total for this request; please
obtain my written approval before exceeding that amount. Contact me
to discuss any necessary clarification or narrowing.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Golden Plasma

communications.subject: Re: Freedom of Information Act Request: RG 330: Research and Development Board finding aids, 1946–1953

communications.subject: Re: [26-96691] Freedom of Information Act Request - Golden Plasma
communications.communication:
Dear Golden Plasma:



This is in response to your Freedom of Information Act request for
information concerning Research and Development Board records found among
the Records of the Office of the Secretary of Defense (Record Group 330)
for the period January 1, 1946, through December 31, 1953. Your request was
received in this office on September 23, 2026, with the assigned control
number 26-96691



As these records are not restricted, they do not require a FOIA request and
are available for you or your representative to review. As part of our
reference service, we provide information about the records, make copies of
the records for a fee, and make records available for use in our research
rooms. The National Archives assists researchers by providing information
for an individual to begin their research. However, we do not generally
conduct research in response to requests (including those filed under the
Freedom of Information Act).



Among the Records of the Office of the Secretary of Defense (Record Group
330) are the following three series of records of the Research and
Development Board:



Records Relating to Organizational Plans and Policies, ca. 1947–1953 (Entry
NM12 341 <https://catalog.archives.gov/id/7065503>)



Transcripts of Meetings, ca. 1947–February 1951 (Entry NM12 342
<https://catalog.archives.gov/id/7065504>)



Progress Reports, ca. 1947–ca. 1953 (Entry NM12 346
<https://catalog.archives.gov/id/7065507>)



The abovementioned record series are further described in our online
catalog. Please click on the links provided for more information. No
additional finding aids are presently available for these records.



Records and their finding aids can be made available to you or your
representative in the Textual Research Room at the National Archives at
College Park, MD <https://www.archives.gov/college-park>. Please visit our
website for information about conducting research at this facility.



Advance research appointments are highly encouraged, but you may also
conduct research as a walk-in. Research appointments can be scheduled via
Eventbrite on the National Archives DC-area Research Appointments page
<https://www.eventbrite.com/o/national-archives-dc-area-research-appointments-87533423643>
.

·        Navigate to Upcoming Events and click on the desired date

·        Click Register and complete the registration process



All researchers must register for a NARA Researcher Card. Researchers are
further encouraged to pre-register in advance of a visit. This process
consists of two parts, including completing the Online Researcher
Orientation <https://share.articulate.com/26AAW-oGjInYSSexGxxb2> and Online
Kiosk Registration
<https://nationalarchives.my.site.com/securitycentral/s/kiosk-registration>
.



Researchers may submit one advanced pull request prior to their scheduled
research visit. To be considered for an advanced pull, researchers must
have a scheduled research appointment and must complete the Online
Researcher Orientation <https://share.articulate.com/26AAW-oGjInYSSexGxxb2>
and Online Kiosk Registration
<https://nationalarchives.my.site.com/securitycentral/s/kiosk-registration>.
To schedule an appointment please visit the National Archives DC-area
Research Appointments
<https://www.eventbrite.com/o/national-archives-dc-area-research-appointments-87533423643>
page.



Advanced pull requests are accepted *7-14 business days* in advance of your
research visit. To submit an advanced pull please send your request to
visit_archives2@nara.gov and include your scheduled visit date.



More information about planning your research visit can be found on our web
pages. Please see the following pertinent information pages:



The National Archives at College Park, Maryland
<https://www.archives.gov/college-park>

Information for Researchers | National Archives
<https://www.archives.gov/college-park/researcher-info>

Self-Service Copying in the Washington, DC, Area Locations | National
Archives <https://www.archives.gov/dc-metro/self-service-copying.html>



If you are unable to come to the National Archives, you may hire a private
researcher to do research for you. A list of private researchers who are
familiar with National Archives facilities is available on our web site at
https://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help/index.html
<http://www.archives.gov/research/hire-help/index.html>.



If you have any additional questions regarding this request, you
may contact us at archives2reference@nara.gov.  We hope you find
this information useful in conducting your research.



This concludes the processing of your request. We do not consider this a
denial of your FOIA request. If you are not satisfied with our action on
this request, your options for appeal and dispute resolution are attached.



Sincerely,



Paul B. Brown



Textual Reference Branch

National Archives at College Park, MD



Attachment

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Kenilworth Nj Police Department)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Kenilworth Nj Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

Please provide responsive records in their original electronic format where reasonably available. For databases, audit logs, search logs, reports, or tabular records, I prefer CSV, XLS/XLSX, or another native machine-readable format rather than PDF printouts.

This request seeks existing government records and does not require the agency to create a new record. If a requested list or summary does not exist as a standalone record, please provide the existing report, export, audit log, configuration record, or other record containing the requested information.

In advance of filing this request, Flock Safety was consulted regarding the availability of these records. Flock Safety indicated that if an agency administrator has difficulty locating relevant audit or system records, the administrator may contact Flock Safety for support.

If any portion of a responsive record is considered exempt from disclosure, please redact only the exempt portion and provide the remainder of the record. Please identify the specific legal basis for each withholding or redaction.

The requested records will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you for your assistance.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 7 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Madthew Pierre-Louis

 We have reviewed our files and have located records that correspond to your request. These records are located at https://url4102.request.justfoia.com/ls/click?upn=u001.nrfdmL-2B1UhWpB4V2ArB2sZTshmi-2FioTkvQmmC7gIeP7OBdYVPVMx2nAXWC0HJ1zhlw8g3mnZ0wGjAX7RAs3b79MW4JNRNggdOFFKA8UJt0M-3DMdzz_virI8lBJSpiH32bdIvSlpOT0eKbldMhm5KOK1iDwV9o8aHBEEf3gaBu17eCfwH7rKoKw-2F1gIQ8Yq70IKeYah-2F3gt5QCA5CQ76LCtaMItxGmqHzUPkzYsYvlkmlX9uW0jJF9rK93SueyzgncHu7IEBT6MwP-2B2e5ToHeWn-2F-2Fg198PqQYSAqMS01BqIXQ7WoaFQ8YKEL6xhPL9QVLBQVQgbUxTW1vKudQLXYrVUqm7LpnfnkgA258N6fSfo-2FQs-2FTEvBYfVcQ-2FAzPMD2bO0qS6vZrJ4z5-2BZIvW5XEeHO-2BBASH1f8yOBTffGE5etvB18ESEWj 
  
 The remainder of your request is denied. In Freidman, the Court focused on the reasonableness standard contemplated throughout the Public Records Law. The Court recognized that the reasonable description requirement is necessary under the Public Records Law because the intent of the law “was not intended to reduce government agencies to full-time investigators on behalf of requestors.” Friedman quoting Assassination Archives & Research Ctr., Inc. v. Central Intelligence Agency, 720 F. Supp. 217, 219 (D.D.C. 1989). 
  
 The additional records that you seek are not organized by this category. Therefore, a records access officer would not have a mechanism of locating the reports without reviewing every record of the Department to determine if it is related. Department employees have no way of reasonably identifying the records you seek without conducting an unreasonable amount of research. Because Department employees would need to conduct extensive research to determine if any records exist, your request does not comply with the Massachusetts Public Records Law and its access regulations. As such, this request is not reasonable and would be overly burdensome on the Department. 
  
 You may appeal this response to the Supervisor of Records in the Office of the Secretary of the Commonwealth. G. L. c. 66, § 10A (c); G. L. c. 66, § 10(b)(ix); 950 CMR 32.08; 950 CMR 32.08(1)(h) (in petitioning the Supervisor, the requester shall provide a copy of such petition to the records access officer associated with such petition). You may also appeal to the Superior Court. 950 CMR 32.06(3)(c). 
  
 Request Number: B-2026-2380 
  
 Thank you.

title: Internal Affairs Complaints & Disciplinary Records (Boston Police Department)

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: Internal Affairs Complaints & Disciplinary Records (Boston Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction regarding disciplinary records from your electronic database from January 2020-June 2026 with the following fields:
IA Number
Incident Type
Date Received
Title/Rank of Officer
First and Last Name of Officer
Officer ID/Badge Number
Summary/Narrative of Complaint 
Allegation
Finding/Outcome
Finding/Completion Date
Action Taken (ie suspension)
Days/Hours Suspended

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2020) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f). 

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

title: Oregon State Police: In-Custody Death Investigation - child killer Richard Wayne Godwin (DOB: ~1945 / Age: 77)

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Oregon State Police: In-Custody Death Investigation - child killer Richard Wayne Godwin (DOB: ~1945 / Age: 77)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law (ORS 192.314 to 192.478), I hereby request copies of all public records, documents, and visual media held, created, or received by the Oregon State Police regarding OSP's involvement in, or assistance with, the in-custody death of Richard Wayne Godwin, who died on or about October 2, 2022, while incarcerated at the Snake River Correctional Institution (SRCI).

I am aware, based on the Oregon Department of Corrections' public news release on this death, that Mr. Godwin passed away in the SRCI infirmary while on hospice care, and that OSP was notified "as with all in-custody deaths" as a matter of standard agency protocol. I recognize this may mean OSP's role was limited to notification and liaison rather than a full criminal investigation. Accordingly, this request is intended to capture whatever record exists documenting OSP's role — whether that is a complete investigative case file or a brief notification/liaison record — and is not limited to records that would only exist if a criminal investigation had been opened.

For guidance, here is a link to an Oregon Department of Corrections press release regarding the in-custody death of Richard Wayne Godwin: 
https://flashalert.net/id/ORCorrections/157984#:~:text=An%20Oregon%20Department%20of%20Corrections%20(DOC)%20adult,11,%202026.%20Godwin%20was%2077%20years%20old

I. SPECIFICALLY REQUESTED RECORDS

Please conduct a search of OSP Major Crimes, Criminal Investigations Division, Detective Division, and Region/Post records for Malheur County / SRCI. This request includes, but is not limited to, the following categories of records, to the extent they exist:

Case Identification: Any OSP case, incident, or report number assigned in connection with this death, and the classification under which the matter was logged (e.g., "Death Investigation," "Non-Criminal Death," "Assist Other Agency," or equivalent).

Investigative Reports & Case Files: All OSP Detective Case Files, initial responder notes, supplementary incident reports, investigative summaries, lead sheets, crime/incident scene processing reports, and administrative logs regarding OSP's involvement or assistance — or, if no formal case file was opened, whatever notification, liaison, or closure memo documents OSP's role and its determination that no further investigation was warranted.

Evidence & Property Logs: Complete evidence ledgers, property receipts, chain-of-custody forms, and lists of physical or digital evidence gathered by OSP personnel, if any were generated.

Interview Audio, Video, & Transcripts: Audio recordings, video recordings, notes, or verbatim transcripts of any witness interviews, inmate/cellmate statements, or staff or medical personnel interviews conducted by OSP officers.

Scene Documentation & Media: a. High-resolution copies of all crime/death scene digital photographs taken by OSP investigators. b. Any surveillance camera or CCTV footage collected by OSP from SRCI or ODOC as evidence.

Communications & Dispatch Records: CAD (Computer Aided Dispatch) event logs, 911/dispatch audio recordings, agency-to-agency notifications (between OSP, ODOC, Malheur County Sheriff's Office, and Malheur County District Attorney), and internal OSP emails or teletypes discussing this matter.

Medical Examiner / Autopsy Correspondence: Copies of any records in OSP's possession from the Oregon State Medical Examiner or Malheur County Medical Examiner concerning the cause and manner of death.

II. STATUTORY TIMELINES & PROCEDURES

Pursuant to ORS 192.329:

Please acknowledge receipt of this request within five (5) business days.

Please complete the processing of this request as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay (statutorily defined as no later than 15 business days following receipt, unless an extension applies under ORS 192.329(5)).

III. SEGREGABILITY AND REDACTION NOTICE

If OSP determines that any portion of the requested records is exempt from disclosure under Oregon law, please note that ORS 192.338 requires the public body to release all non-exempt, reasonably segregable portions of the records.

If any document, photograph, or media file is withheld or redacted in full or in part:

Identify the specific statutory exemption claimed for each redaction or withholding — for example, ORS 192.355(2)(b) (images of a dead body) or ORS 192.345(36) (medical examiner reports), as applicable — rather than a general citation to Oregon public records law.

Provide a brief description of the material withheld.

State the basis for applying the exemption to a death that occurred in October 2022, where no criminal proceedings resulted and the subject is deceased. For any withholding under ORS 192.355(2)(b) specifically, please address whether the public interest in disclosure — including public oversight of ODOC's hospice and infirmary care and OSP's protocols for reviewing custodial deaths — outweighs the privacy interest the exemption is meant to protect.

IV. FEE WAIVER / PUBLIC INTEREST REQUEST

Pursuant to ORS 192.324(5), I request a reduction or complete waiver of any processing fees. Release of these records primarily benefits the general public by fostering transparency, oversight, and public confidence in the administration of justice, state law enforcement operations, and the conditions and quality of medical/hospice care within Oregon Department of Corrections facilities. This request is made for public oversight and historical/educational research, not for commercial use.

If a fee waiver is denied and the estimated fees to fulfill this request exceed $25.00, please provide an itemized estimate of the costs prior to commencing work, as required by ORS 192.324(4)(c).

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware

communications.subject: Colorado Open Records Act Request: Correspondence Between DOS and ALPR Vendors
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

I am looking for a few pieces of information related to:
CR26-0246, a contract between the city of Denver and Axon Enterprise Inc. allowing for the purchase and install of multiple ALPR Units (https://denver.legistar.com/LegislationDetail.aspx?ID=7938541&GUID=093F64CB-3951-4C69-9B4B-14B57D302CA6&Options=&Search=)
Denver Police Department had a pilot program and then a contract with Flock Safety that the police found very useful. They then cancelled that contract and entered into a new contract with Axon Enterprise Inc. I'm hoping to find out what about the old system or the old vendor police and/or city leadership didn't like, as well as what they do like about this new system. I’d also like to find out what the police hoped to get out of the old system, how they talked about it internally, and what they are hoping to get out of the new system.

Please provide the following: 

1. The planned locations, or current locations of the ALPR Units from contract POLIC-202683606

2. Contract POLIC-202683606

3. Correspondence (emails, memos, instant messages, etc.) sent internally or DPD/DOS employee to Vendors of ALPR’s.
To reduce the burden and scope of this request, please limit correspondence to items dated between Jan 1, 2022 to the time this request is processed.
To further reduce the burden and scope of the request, limit correspondence with ALPR vendors to employees or parties representing Flock Safety and Axon Enterprise, Inc. (for emails: addresses ending in @flocksafety.com; @axon.com)
To further reduce the burden and scope of the request, please return correspondence with subject line or contents including key phrases such as:
Flock
Flock Safety
25-0413
ALPR
LPR
LPR's
Axon ALPR
Axon LPR
CR26-0246
CR 26-0246
CR 26 0246
26-0246
POLIC-202683606
202683606
Surveillance
Surveillance Task Force

Finally, to further limit the burden and scope of this request, limit correspondence to items where the following parties are either a sender or recipient:
Ron Thomas, Chief of Police
Al Gardner, Deputy Mayor
Emily Lauck, Policy Director
Commander Cliff Barnes, Director of DPD Cyber Bureau
Jacob Hererra
Todd Ericson

For email and other applicable mediums of correspondence, please include attachments.

I appreciate the possibility that even after the attempted limiting of scope and burden, there may still be a considerable amount of items that fit this request. Please let me know if this is the case and I will do my best to further refine the scope of the search.

Thank you for your help,
William Beckett
Resident of the Baker Neighborhood, Denver

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

William Beckett

Good afternoon-

This email is being sent in response to your CORA request submitted on May 20, 2026. Please find the Department’s responses to each item of your request outlined below.

  1.
The planned locations, or current locations of the ALPR Units from contract POLIC-20268360

Please visit https://denvergov.org/Government/Agencies-Departments-Offices/Agencies-Departments-Offices-Directory/Police-Department/Safety-and-Crime-Prevention/Auto-Theft-Prevention and navigate to "Additional Resources” on the right-hand side, where you will find the ALPR locations map.

  1.
Contract POLIC-202683606

See attached.

  1.  Correspondence (emails, memos, instant messages, etc.) sent internally or DPD/DOS employee to Vendors of ALPR’s between Jan 1, 2022 to the time this request is processed

Our initial system search returned approximately 69,000 potentially responsive items based upon the search terms you provided. This number reflects all automated system matches and will need to be significantly narrowed to identify the actual correspondence requiring review. Depending upon the nature of the communications, redactions of information may also be necessary.



Based on typical review rates (approximately 15 minutes per correspondence item), the review of records associated with this search volume could require several hundred staff hours, depending on how many of the system matches are ultimately unique, responsive communications. Using the standard CORA labor rate ($41.37 per hour), the rough cost estimate for completing this work is approximately $21,000.



This estimate is preliminary and may change as we refine the dataset, remove duplicate items, exclude automated notices, and identify non‑responsive material. The total cost may also decrease if you choose to narrow the scope of your request.



Best,

I believe in the most recent search performed, there was no discrimination between correspondences where at least one of the 7 listed custodians was either the sender or the reciever. Or at least, the screenshot of the search results seem to suggest that.

If a more accurate search was able to be performed earlier on 6/10/2026 but can no longer be performed now, and Elizabeth White or the Technology Services team can't be reached, would you be available to talk via phonecall to more quickly narrow down the scope of my request? I don't want to give any undue work to you or your department, and I am confident we can reduce the scope of the request to be reasonable to execute.

Thank you/as always for your continued attention to this matter,
William Beckett

title: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Westfield Police Department)

communications.subject: New Jersey Open Public Records Act Request: Flock Safety ALPR Use Across Union County, NJ — Audit Logs, Searches & Data Sharing (Westfield Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New Jersey Open Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

For the period July 20, 2026 through August 19, 2026, please provide:

1. Records showing the total number of license plates, vehicle detections, or plate reads captured or scanned through Flock Safety ALPR systems accessible to or operated by the department.

2. The names of all hot lists, watch lists, alert lists, or similar lists used, enabled, or accessible through the department’s Flock Safety system.

3. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities with which the department shares Flock Safety ALPR data.

4. A list of all law enforcement agencies, government entities, organizations, or other entities from which the department receives or has access to Flock Safety ALPR data.

5. All agreements, memoranda of understanding, contracts, arrangements, or other records concerning access to Flock Safety cameras, systems, or data owned, funded, or operated by homeowner associations, private businesses, private organizations, or individuals.

6. All current contracts, memoranda of understanding, agreements, amendments, renewals, statements of work, or similar agreements between the department, municipality, or other applicable public entity and Flock Safety.

7. All procurement records related to Flock Safety, including purchase orders, invoices, bids, quotes, proposals, requisitions, payment records, and records reflecting the purchase, lease, subscription, acquisition, installation, or renewal of Flock Safety equipment or services.

8. All audit logs, search logs, query logs, usage reports, or similar records relating to the department’s use of Flock Safety ALPR systems during the requested period, including but not limited to:

- Records of license plate or vehicle searches performed by agency personnel;
- Dates and timestamps of searches;
- User identification associated with searches, including names, badge numbers, usernames, or user IDs, where maintained;
- Case numbers, incident numbers, investigation references, reasons, or purposes associated with searches, where maintained;
- Records showing networks or agencies whose Flock data is shared with or accessible to the department;
- Records showing networks or agencies to which the department shares its Flock data;
- Event logs, system activity logs, or audit records reflecting changes to hot lists, watch lists, alerts, users, permissions, or network-sharing settings;
- Records showing changes to data-sharing relationships or network access; and
- Records reflecting live-stream, live-view, camera access, or similar access permissions and configuration settings, if applicable.

This request specifically includes records available through Flock Safety features or reports identified as “Organization Audit,” “Network Audit,” or equivalent audit, usage, sharing, or administrative reports available within the Flock Safety platform, including the “Insights” section where applicable.

9. Records showing the department’s current Flock Safety network-sharing configuration, including which networks, agencies, or organizations share data with the department and which networks, agencies, or organizations receive data from the department.

10. Screenshots, exports, reports, or other existing records reflecting relevant Flock Safety configuration settings, including network-sharing settings and live-stream/live-view access settings, to the extent such records are maintained by the agency.

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: IHSC SENs and SIRs
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

An IHSC record showing the number, by month and year if possible, of Significant Event Notifications (SENs), Significant Incident Reports (SIRs), or similar records IHSC received for the period beginning January 1, 2021, and continuing through May 5, 2025, in which ICE ERO Field Office staff, ICE detention contractors, or IHSC Field Medical Coordinators who submitted the SEN or SIR checked the box next to "Death in Custody or Operations", "Hospital Admission," "Emergency Department Visit (ED", or "Serious Health Incidents Affected Bedspace Volume".

Here is an example of SEN/SIR data from a single ICE detention facility provided in response to a prior FOIA: https://www.documentcloud.org/documents/25469567-aurora-medical-sens-sirs-2023-icfo-03979-001/. I am seeking a report from the IHSC system of records the government's detention medical supervisors use to track and monitor these SENs and SIRs at facilities nationwide. I am willing to discuss narrowing or altering this requests should IHSC have a more efficient means of providing something similar to allow for data analysis. 

I seek expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and declare under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 U.S.C. 1746 that the following statements are true and correct to the best of my knowledge and understanding: 
1. I am a member of the media primarily engaged in information dissemination, and I have been granted expedited processing on this basis previously by federal FOIA agencies.  Examples of my edited works are available here: https://theappeal.org/authors/andrew-free/, here: https://atlpresscollective.com/author/free/, and here: https://assets.aclu.org/live/uploads/2024/06/2024-07-01-ICE-Detainee-Deaths.pdf. 
2. As ICE has rapidly increased its detained noncitizen population since January 2025, mortality in ICE custody has also rapidly increased. 
3. ICE is presently on track to allow more people to die in the agency's custody than in any year since FY2020, when the COVID19 pandemic ripped through facilities claiming lives until federal judges ordered targeted depopulation over ICE's objections. 

Table 1: Publicly Reported Deaths in ICE Custody by Fiscal Year since PBNDS 2011 adoption.
FY	COUNT of FY
11	10
12	8
13	9
14	6
15	7
16	10
17	12
18	10
19	9
20	22
21	5
22	3
23	4
24	12
25	10

4. Public reports indicate Congress intends to appropriate a roughly 900% increase in ICE detention funding, spending $45 billion to expand the deadly detention system. https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/07/us/politics/trump-administration-immigrant-detention-facilities-services.html. 
5. Timely access to information regarding healthcare outcomes in ICE custody is essential to public health researchers, medical experts, policymakers, and informed citizens who wish to have a meaningful role in the policy debate over whether the proposed budget increase represents a lawful and prudent expenditure of public resources. 
6. My previous FOIA work on ICE detention morbidity and mortality has resulted in obtaining records that have been shared with and cited by physicians, oversight agencies, Congress, and courts, influencing decisions that led to healthier outcomes for ICE's detained populations, and reducing the morbidity and mortality in ICE custody. 
7. There is an urgent need to inform the public regarding IHSC's capacity to manage and oversee medical emergencies and conditions that could lead to deaths of people in ICE custody. 

I respectfully request a fee waiver, as I will be publishing and circulating the results of the records I receive, and am not making this request for commercial purposes. 

Thank you in advance for your timely consideration of this time-sensitive request.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: ICE Death Records - Francisco
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

ICE detainee death records for Carlos Juan Francisco, a 42 year-old migrant from Guatemala, who died following his detention at the Krome Detention Center on December 4, 2023 (see https://www.ice.gov/doclib/foia/reports/ddr_carlosJuanFrancisco.pdff): 

1. The Office of Professional Responsibility Detainee Death Review (search the External Reviews and Analysis Unit within ICE OPR); 
2. The Creative Corrections Healthcare and Security Compliance Analysis report (search ERAU); 
3. the IHSC Mortality Review (search the ICE Health Service Corps); 
4. The IHSC Root Cause Analysis, if any (search IHSC). 

We request expedited processing of this request pursuant to 6 C.F.R. 5.5(e) and provide the following statements in support of our request under penalty of perjury pursuant to 28 USC 1746: 

1. At the time of this request, ICE deaths in custody have doubled the highest levels from previous years of the Biden administration. https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-double-last-year-rcna154659#:~:text=NBC%20News%20Tipline-,The%20number%20of%20deaths%20in%20ICE%20custody%20is%20already%20more,of%20the%20six%20preceding%20years.
2. The current rate of in-custody ICE deaths is on track to exceed any non-COVID year since FY17. See: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11007418/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7870381/
3. Deaths in ICE custody have been the subject of widespread, ongoing media coverage and extensive policy advocacy and discussion. See, e.g. ,https://www.npr.org/2023/11/08/1211316303/ice-releases-investigation-into-immigrants-death-after-months-of-inexcusable-del; https://www.yahoo.com/news/number-deaths-ice-custody-already-133000592.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAALCThkPLfU2ufNLo_I3yqmeUO38qEyUSI4U597M71FTc3npyfor0xVw-REfCt-2anUv5517ufGPQZZuU4KKiJ98axkk_ivGQf5e9Gu_gYZaHzjunplOd3-7tEQTfDoPBn6g0zjNvYt8aKSYJBBN9iLv2gvnes6k94yMIMemD-0yw; https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/30/us/migrant-death-ice-custody-recommended-release/index.html.
4. There exist serious questions regarding the government's capacity to ensure safe and humane detention conditions that prevent deaths in ICE custody, based on available FOIA records obtained through federal litigation.  See, e.g., https://prismreports.org/2023/04/20/ice-gourgan-mirimanian-death-2018/; https://today.usc.edu/ice-deaths-custody-detention-medical-standards-violated-usc-study/
5. ICE has announced its intention to expand its detention system, potentially increasing the numbers of in-custody death to even higher levels. https://www.ice.gov/news/releases/ice-announces-ongoing-work-optimize-enforcement-resources
6. ICE has previously failed to accurately inform the public of its own internal agency conclusions about the events leading up to in-custody deaths. See, e.g., https://www.aclu.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/April-2024-ACLU-Letter-to-ICE-on-Torrance-Detention-Facility.pdf

There is a compelling need to obtain these records as soon as possible so that the public can understand the consequences of ICE's current detention management processes as the agency seeks to expand the system beyond its appropriated limit of 41,500 beds.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Andrew Free

title: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep (Lafayette Parish Sheriff's Office)

communications.subject: Louisiana Public Records Law Request: LexisNexis Community Crime Map Contributors - Initial Sweep (Lafayette Parish Sheriff's Office)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Louisiana Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

This request is related to the Community Crime Map (CCM) and Accurint, both are products of LexisNexis. You are receiving this request because your agency's name was listed on the crime map available at communitycrimemap.com. We are seeking documents about how your agency integrates with LexisNexis to provide anonymized data to the CCM, and whether your agency shares de-anonymized data with local, state, and federal law enforcement agencies via Accurint Virtual Crime Center (AVCC) or Public Safety Data Exchange (PSDEx). If your agency currently or previously shared data with LexisNexis, please provide the below documents.  

We are requesting:
1) Technical integration documents: Any documents, integrations instructions, tutorials, and similar documents from LexisNexis about how to connect your RMS/CAD/JMS systems to LexisNexis's systems. [Typically held by IT or records systems teams/vendors from when your agency originally integrated with LexisNexis's systems]
2) Agreements: The signed "XML Addendum", Database Interface Agreement, or similar legal agreement that dictates how your agency's data may be used and shared. [Typically held by legal or procurement departments]
3) Shared Data: An export of what data you share with CCM and other law enforcement agencies. This is often called a Data Classification Crime Results sheet. To obtain this, an account admin can click a link on the left-hand side under admin permissions called 'Data Classification Manager.' There is an Export link on the top right of the Data Classification Manager page. Depending on the LexisNexis product(s) you subscribe to, this may have a different name or location. We are looking for the list of data you share with LexisNexis, and who your share it with (CCM only, or also other law enforcement agencies?) [Only an CCM/Accurint Account Administrators can access these documents]

If you want examples of what these documents look like from other agencies, or you would like suggested search terms to find these documents - please don't hesitate to reach out.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Shawn Segal

communications.subject: Nevada Public Records Act Request: LVMPD Price Retention
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Nevada Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

This is a new request and is narrower than, and distinct from, my request of 17 May 2026, reference X010952-051726, which your office closed on 19 May 2026 with the response "No records were located."

I am not seeking the case file. I am seeking the Department's own records governing the retention and disposition of records of that type and era:

1. The records retention and disposition schedule or schedules in effect for LVMPD incident, event, case and death-investigation reports generated in 1975, together with any subsequent schedule that governed the disposition of 1975-era reports.

2. Any certificate of destruction, destruction log, disposal authorization, or equivalent record documenting the destruction or other disposition of LVMPD incident, event or case reports from calendar year 1975.

3. Any record describing the transfer of 1975-era LVMPD reports to another custodian, including the Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records, or any successor agency, and the date of any such transfer.

4. Any policy, procedure or index describing where 1975-era LVMPD records are currently held, if they are held at all.

These records are separate from the case file that was the subject of the earlier request. My earlier request asked, in the alternative, for destruction documentation and retention authority, and the 19 May response did not address that portion. Whether the report never existed or was lawfully destroyed on a schedule are different facts, and this request seeks the records that establish which is the case.

If any portion is exempt, please identify the specific statutory basis for the withholding as required by NRS 239.0107.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jerome McClure

communications.subject: Massachusetts Public Records Law Request: AER - MA Department of Public Health
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Massachusetts Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

All adverse medical event records filed with the Massachusetts Department of Public Health between Jan. 1, 2023 and Jan. 1, 2025.

I request these records in their native digital formats and not in formats that degrade the accessibility of the records, such as tabular data converted to PDF or Word files. If converting the native digital format to another high-fidelity format, such as CSV or Excel, please take care not to introduce formatting inconsistencies or errors, which can occur in the conversion process (for example, encoding errors or the inclusion of internal unescaped quotation marks in CSV files). Should the records above represent certain values as numeric codes or abbreviations that are not self-explanatory, we additionally request all records necessary to interpret those codes and abbreviations.

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Michael Nolan

title: City of Bixby Opioid Settlement Funds

communications.subject: Oklahoma Open Records Act Request: City of Bixby Opioid Settlement Funds
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Under the Oklahoma Open Records Act, 51 §24A.1 et seq., I request an opportunity to inspect or obtain copies of public records related to the allocation and use of opioid lawsuit settlement funds in the City of Bixby. Specifically, I am seeking:

1. Documentation of the amount of opioid settlement funds your office has received thus far from the Oklahoma Attorney General’s Office as a non-litigating political subdivision. 
2. Records detailing which individuals and/or programs have been awarded a portion of your opioid lawsuit settlement funds. 
3. Any documentation related to the review or approval process to apply for funding, including the names and organizations of individuals involved in the application process. 
4. Minutes of any public meetings or hearings, including public officials, in which opioid settlement fund allocation was discussed. 
5. Any correspondence and attachments between county officials regarding the allocation or use of these funds. 

If there are any fees for searching or copying these records, please inform me if the cost will exceed $25.00. However, I would also like to request a waiver of all fees, as disclosure of the requested information is in the public interest. This request is related to news-gathering purposes; it is not being sought for commercial purposes.

If you expect a significant delay in responding to or in fulfilling this request, please contact me with information about when I might expect copies or the ability to inspect the requested records.

I look forward to receiving your response to this request. Thank you for the help, and please let me know if you have any questions. 

Sincerely, 

Sierra Pfeifer | KOSU
Mental health & addiction reporter
sierra@kosu.org | 919-448-5430

title: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Employment Information (Graham Police Department)

communications.subject: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: North Carolina Public Records Law Request: Employment Information (Graham Police Department)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the North Carolina Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Employment information for all sworn law enforcement officers employed from the dates: 1950–present. Specifically, I request the following public information for each officer: Full name, Date of original employment/appointment, position title and history of position changes, dates of promotions, demotions, transfers. 

If possible, please provide this data in electronic format, Excel or CSV, database, via email attachment or CD-ROM if email is not feasible.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Alex Noll

communications.subject: Public Records Response
communications.communication:
RESPONSE TO PUBLIC RECORDS ACT REQUEST – CITY CLERK
(CA. Gov’t Code §7920.000 et seq.)


Re: PUBLIC RECORDS ACT REQUEST RECEIVED ON ­Monday, August 10, 2026

The City of Santa Cruz responds to your public records request for information received on ­Monday, August 10, 2026, as indicated below.

Under the California Public Records Act (CPRA) you are entitled to copies of identifiable, non-exempt public records (Govt. Code section 7922.530). Please note that the CPRA requires the City to provide access to, or copies of, records responsive to your request which are in its possession, subject to certain exceptions. The CPRA does not require the City to provide information, answer questions, or create records which do not exist.

Records Requested:
“Please provide all contracts, MOUs, and invoices related to Placer Labs, Inc. between January 1, 2023 and August 10, 2026.”

The City has extended its time to respond to your request to ­Thursday, September 3, 2026 pursuant to the California Public Records Act, Government section 7920.000 et seq. (the “CPRA”), for the following reason:

☒ Government Code § 7922.535(c)(3) • The need for consultation, which shall be conducted with all practicable speed, with another agency having substantial interest in the determination of the request or among two or more components of the agency having substantial subject matter interest therein.

We appreciate your patience while we process your request. Please feel free to reach out with any questions.

Thank you,

Brittany Inclan
Records Coordinator
City of Santa Cruz | City Manager’s Office | City Clerk’s Division
809 Center Street, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
Direct: 831-420-5034
Email: binclan@santacruzca.gov
Web: santacruzca.gov<https://www.cityofsantacruz.com/>
[cid:image001.png@01DD30A5.40587920]

Public Records Act Requests may be submitted online via the Public Records Request form or by hard copy form available at the City Clerk’s Office located at 809 Center Street, Room 8, Santa Cruz, CA 95060.

Please note: Public Record Act Requests submitted via email, fax, USPS, or drop off after 5:00 p.m. on a business day, Saturdays, Sundays, or holidays will be processed as received on the next open business day. The 10-day response period begins when the request is received.
